result.title: SkillBrowser: Selective Skill Exposure for Scalable Skill-Using Agents
result.comment: 23 pages, 3 figures. Submitted to ACL Rolling Review, October 2026
result.summary: Large language model agents increasingly rely on skills to extend their capabilities in complex tasks. However, scalable skill use requires Selective Skill Exposure (SSE): providing relevant procedural content when needed while avoiding unnecessary exposure that may disrupt reasoning. Existing paradigms fall short in complementary ways. Progressive disclosure exposes metadata for a growing skill library, introducing context pollution; retrieval limits catalog exposure, but static retrieval from the initial task query may be misaligned with capability needs that emerge during reasoning and may still inject unnecessary skills. We propose SkillBrowser, a Meta-Skill-managed framework that enables an agent to identify current capability needs, formulate targeted queries, and selectively load skills on demand. Across six SRA-Bench subsets and five LLMs, SkillBrowser improves aggregate accuracy over static retrieval and LLM-based selection, including multi-step tool use, and mitigates accuracy degradation on already-solvable instances. Benefits remain model- and task-dependent, with under-invocation of useful skills and additional latency as key limitations. These results demonstrate the viability of Meta-Skill-managed SSE for scalable skill repositories.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 SkillBrowser：由 Meta-Skill 管理的框架，让智能体在推理中识别当前能力需求、生成针对性查询并按需加载技能，在 SRA-Bench 六个子集与五种 LLM 上优于静态检索和 LLM 选择，并报告技能欠调用与额外延迟等代价。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按需识别能力缺口再获取外部内容」及对额外延迟、调用不足的显式核算，可能与 LVR 中 LOOK/证据获取与停止决策的收益-成本权衡形成概念联系，属推测，可供核查是否能迁移到视觉证据筛选。
